title: AlphaGo: Mastering the Game of Go
hook: Go has more board positions than atoms in the universe, and experts thought superhuman play was a decade off. AlphaGo beat a top professional in 2016.
key_points: Combined deep neural networks with Monte Carlo tree search to play Go at superhuman level.
A policy network suggests promising moves; a value network estimates who's winning from a position.
Learned from human expert games and then improved through self-play reinforcement learning.
Defeated a top professional player, a milestone many expected was still years away.
content_html: David Silver, Aja Huang, and the DeepMind team built AlphaGo, the first program to play Go at a superhuman level. Go's enormous branching factor had long defeated the brute-force search that conquered chess, so AlphaGo paired deep neural networks with Monte Carlo tree search to focus its thinking. It learned from a large set of human expert games and then sharpened itself through self-play, and in 2016 it beat a top professional — a result many believed was still a decade away.
extra_html:
How it works

AlphaGo uses two neural networks. A policy network looks at a board and proposes which moves are worth considering, pruning the otherwise impossibly wide search. A value network estimates the chance of winning from a given position, so the program doesn't have to play every line to the end. These guide a Monte Carlo tree search that explores promising sequences. The networks were first trained to imitate strong human play, then improved by playing many games against versions of themselves.

Why it matters

Go was a long-standing symbol of the gap between human intuition and machine search, precisely because good play seemed to require pattern recognition rather than calculation. AlphaGo's win showed that learned evaluation plus guided search could capture that intuition, and it became a defining public moment for deep reinforcement learning. It set the stage for more general successors that needed no human game data at all.

related.title: AlphaZero: Mastering Games from Scratch
related.hook: AlphaGo learned from human games. AlphaZero threw those away — one algorithm reached superhuman chess, shogi, and Go knowing only the rules and playing itself.

related.title: AlphaFold: Protein Structure Prediction
related.hook: Predicting a protein's 3D shape from its sequence stumped biology for ~50 years. AlphaFold cracked it at near-experimental accuracy — and then released the structures to everyone.
